source_spans.locator: Psychological Review 92(3), published p.289 abstract and pp.289-290 opening thesis: insufficient constraint from feature-overlap accounts; proposed dependence of class coherence on background knowledge
Psychological Review 92(3), published pp.291-297, insufficiency-of-similarity discussion: unconstrained properties/weights admit arbitrary groupings and fail to determine coherence

Psychological Review 92(3), published pp.298-299, 'Concepts as Embedded in Theories' and Tables 1-2: explanatory relations constrain relevant properties; internal and external structure are distinguished
Psychological Review 92(3), published pp.313-314, concluding synthesis: two components of coherence are internal relational structure and fit with the broader knowledge base

conditions: a candidate class is being evaluated for why its members form a comprehensible grouping

nodes.description: degree to which the members of a candidate class form a comprehensible and usable grouping
background domain knowledge containing explanatory, causal, or other relations among items and classes
relations among properties internal to the candidate class
integration of the candidate class with other knowledge in the broader knowledge base
other possible groupings left admissible when an account does not sufficiently constrain relevant properties and relations

relations.description: the coherence of a candidate grouping depends on its fit with background explanatory knowledge
coherence depends on both internal relational organization and integration with the broader knowledge base
background explanatory knowledge constrains which internal properties and relations are treated as relevant and how they are organized
adding explanatory relations limits the otherwise broad set of possible groupings admitted by weak property-overlap accounts
